Life OS: a life operating system that runs your day

A life OS, or life operating system, is one personal system that holds your goals, routines, commitments and rules, so you run your life from the system instead of from memory. Many people build one as a Notion template; others want one that plans and follows up for them.

Quick answer

A life OS works when it decides the next step for you and keeps going after a bad day. Templates hold information; A Player Mode runs it: it builds a Mind, Body, Spirit plan from a few easy taps and has your day ready every morning.

Best for: People who have built a Notion life OS or a personal operating system and found they stopped opening it.

What goes into a life OS?

Your areas of life, your goals in each, your routines and the rules that keep you on track.

  • Mind: work, business and career, money, learning, focus and mental health.
  • Body: movement, food, sleep, weight and health routines.
  • Spirit: faith, meditation, gratitude, nature, service, family and relationships.
  • Rules: your minimum day, your non-negotiables and what happens after a miss.

These are A Player Mode's three pillars, on by default, so the basics are covered without you deciding to cover them.

Why do most life OS templates stop working?

A template stores the plan but never runs it: you still have to open it, decide and remember.

The work of a life OS is the daily part: choosing today's priority, following up and recovering after a bad day. A template leaves that to you. A Player Mode does it: one priority each morning, a short start, then the day, and after a miss it shrinks the next day instead of adding catch-up.

How do you set up a life OS with A Player Mode?

In about 3 minutes, by answering easy-tap questions.

  1. Answer easy-tap questions: about 3 minutes to a working plan. Stop any time; nothing is lost.
  2. It builds your Mind, Body, Spirit plan and Tracks: your goals, your rules and your minimum day. You approve each piece.
  3. It runs your day: every morning your plan is ready. Bad days shrink automatically.

Tracks are background filters that shape every plan, such as Operator Discipline, Strategic Patience, Resilience or Home Front. APM suggests the ones that fit; you approve them and can switch any off.

Frequently asked questions

What is a personal operating system?

A personal operating system is the same idea as a life OS: a set of rules, routines and one place for your commitments, so your days follow a system rather than your mood. A Player Mode is a personal operating system that plans and follows up for you.

Can I build a life OS in Notion?

Yes, and many people do. A Notion life OS is good at holding information. What it does not do is plan your day, follow up on promises or adjust after a bad day; you do that yourself each time you open it. A Player Mode does those parts for you.
